evidence: 0x461b50 main allocates a Lua state, passes argv/argc to protected pmain at 0x4021a0, reports errors and closes the state.
pmain handles standard -e/-l/-b/-j/-O/-i/-E options; 0x402794 reads LUA_INIT, then dispatches an @file or inline script. No fixed startup payload was found.
0x429f30 changes protection of the JIT code area; the other VirtualProtect uses include MinGW relocation support.
TLS callbacks 0x45ee50/0x45ee00 perform CRT TLS initialization/cleanup; TerminateProcess at 0x45ede9 targets GetCurrentProcess on a CRT failure path.
The 4,693 trailing bytes begin at the COFF symbol-table offset and contain 129 symbols plus their string table. No appended executable payload was identified.
Imports are KERNEL32.dll and msvcrt.dll. The luajit.org URL is in the version banner. No networking startup, embedded hostile Lua, or concealed download path was found.
samples.label_explanation: The supplied detection names MisusedLegit.LuaJIT: a legitimate interpreter may be collected alongside malicious scripts; the executable alone does not establish that abuse.

evidence: Fresh Go-proxy download is byte-identical to the supplied archive.
make.ps1 dispatches local CMake build/configure/install and test commands. Its outDir paths identify locally built tests, not downloaded scripts.
registry.py and ghcr_nightly.py exchange GITHUB_TOKEN for GHCR authorization and transfer build cache or release archives; no unrelated credential destination or collection path was found.
DragonFly provisioning downloads an official BSD image, launches QEMU and uses a generated SSH key with loopback port 2222 to provision the guest.

The bundled regression-4613 ELF has source whose Main constructor does nothing. Disassembly of main at 0x5800 initializes Pony, creates the actor and starts the runtime; Main_Dispatch at 0x3b20 only performs receive/GC bookkeeping.
LLVM is pinned to fc4aad7b5db3fff421df9a9637605b9ca5667881. Fetched its CMake source and the benchmark/googletest source archives; inspected build and test context.
Pony tuple syntax and generic calls in .pony files were being parsed as JavaScript sequence expressions and computed calls.
samples.label_explanation: Likely static build/runtime capability and source-language false positives. The exact external labeling rationale is not established.

evidence: Fresh Go-proxy download is byte-identical to the supplied archive.
Architecture-specific Go files implement libc syscall/CRT wrappers and ccgo-generated C translations. SYS_memfd_create and SYS_finit_module matches are syscall-number declarations in headers.
readdir64/access/lstat matches occur in API declarations and ABI shim source, not concealed replacement hooks.
Start constructs argv/environment and calls the caller-provided C main. Platform initialization sets runtime structures, allocator data, and standard streams.

Xsystem passes its caller-provided command to sh -c; socket/connect/chmod wrappers perform the requested OS operation. No autonomous collection, attacker endpoint, or malicious initializer was identified.
Fetched all 22 declared Go module dependencies, scanned them and reviewed initializer behavior, runtime wrappers and generator/build-tool execution context.
samples.label_explanation: Likely runtime capability false positives: libc necessarily exposes networking, process creation, memory and filesystem APIs. No concrete hostile behavior was found.
